At age 89 in 2023, this Spanish economist and former Communist politician was proposed as a prime ministerial candidate in a Vox-led no-confidence vote — who is he?
Ramón Tamames: Spanish economist and politician. Ramón Tamames Gómez (born 1 November 1933) is a Spanish economist and former politician.
This British lawyer-turned-diplomat was one of the architects of the League of Nations, and his lifelong defense of it earned him the 1937 Nobel Peace Prize — who was he?
Robert Cecil, Viscount Cecil of Chelwood
Robert Cecil, Viscount Cecil of Chelwood: British lawyer, politician and diplomat (1864–1958)
Robert Cecil, Viscount Cecil of Chelwood
A member of Japan's Democratic Party, this politician served in the House of Representatives of the national Diet until his death in 2018 — who is he?
The youngest person and first woman ever elected governor of Alaska, she was the Republican Party's vice presidential nominee alongside John McCain in 2008 — who is she?
Princess Alice of the United Kingdom
At just 13 he became the youngest sole emperor of the united Roman Empire, succeeding his slain cousin Elagabalus as the last ruler of the Severan dynasty. Who was he?
Severus Alexander: Roman emperor from 222 to 235.
Founded in 1905 by Arthur Griffith, this Irish party's members established the revolutionary First Dáil and fought in the War of Independence — which party?
Sinn Féin: Political party in Ireland.
A former Mathematical Economics professor at IIT Delhi known for Hindu nationalist views, he led the Janata Party until 2013 before joining the BJP — who is this Indian politician?
Subramanian Swamy: Indian politician. Subramanian Swamy (born 15 September 1939) is an Indian politician, economist and statistician.
This form of governance grounds legitimacy in scientific and technical expertise rather than the rule of the people — what's it called?
Technocracy: Form of government ruled by experts.

Governed by the Ganden Phodrang and declared independent by the 13th Dalai Lama after the Qing dynasty's collapse in 1912, this East Asian state was annexed by the People's Republic of China in 1951 — which state?
Tibet (1912–1951): Former de facto state in East Asia.

Known as the Risorgimento, this 19th-century movement folded numerous peninsular states into the Kingdom of Sardinia in 1861 and finished in 1871 when Rome became the new nation's capital — what was it?
Unification of Italy: 1848–1870 consolidation of Italian states.
Led first by Alaric I, this Gothic people sacked Rome in 410 before founding a kingdom centered on Toulouse and later Spain — who were they?
Visigoths: Germanic people of late antiquity and the early Middle Ages.
A Rhodes Scholar and former U.S. Army officer, this author-turned-politician became Maryland's 63rd governor in 2023 — who is he?
A Polish soldier-statesman who fought in the Polish Legions and played a prominent role in the 1920 Battle of Warsaw, he later served as prime minister of the Second Polish Republic. Who was he?
Władysław Sikorski: Polish military and political leader (1881–1943)
Ruling from Mount Olympus as king of the gods, this son of Cronus and Rhea fathered Athena, Apollo, and Heracles among many others. Who is this Greek deity?
Zeus: Greek god of the sky and king of the gods.
Which one below was born first?
Qian Xuesen (born 1911) is the earliest of the four. Qian received his undergraduate education in mechanical engineering at National Chiao Tung University in Shanghai in 1934.
Which of these four was born earliest?
Emanuel Swedenborg (born 1688) is the earliest of the four. Swedenborg had a prolific career as an inventor and scientist.
Which one below was born first?
Levi Strauss (born 1829) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four came first?
C++ (founded 1983) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the astronomer from these four.
Jane Luu is an astronomer. Luu (Vietnamese: Lưu Lệ Hằng; born July 1963) is a Vietnamese-American astronomer and defense systems engineer.
Pick the mathematician from these four.
Jim Simons is a mathematician. James Harris Simons (April 25, 1938 – May 10, 2024) was an American hedge fund manager, investor, mathematician, and philanthropist.
What is the atomic number of Niobium?
Niobium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nb (formerly columbium, Cb) and atomic number 41.
What is the atomic number of Phosphorus?
Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.
In what year was Émile Durkheim born?
Émile Durkheim: David Émile Durkheim (French: [emil dyʁkɛm] or [dyʁkajm]; 15 April 1858 – 15 November 1917) was a French sociologist.
In what year was Gregor Mendel born?
Gregor Mendel: Mendel worked with seven characteristics of pea plants: plant height, pod shape and colour, seed shape and colour, and flower position and colour.
In what year was Leonhard Euler born?
Leonhard Euler: Euler has been called a "universal genius" who "was fully equipped with almost unlimited powers of imagination, intellectual gifts and extraordinary memory".
In what year did Alexander Hamilton die?
Alexander Hamilton: Born out of wedlock in Charlestown on the Caribbean island of Nevis, Hamilton was orphaned as a child and taken in by a prosperous merchant.
In what year did Kitty O'Neil die?
Kitty O'Neil: O'Neil subsequently moved into car racing and became a pioneering woman in the stunt industry in Hollywood.
In what year was Huntington's disease discovered?
Huntington's disease (HD), also known as Huntington's chorea, is a fatal neurodegenerative disease that is usually inherited.
Swift (programming language): Apple Inc. Swift compiles to machine code and uses an LLVM-based compiler.
Levofloxacin: Pfizer. Levofloxacin, sold under the brand name Levaquin among others, is a broad-spectrum antibiotic of the fluoroquinolone drug class.
Publishing: Germany. It has various divisions such as trade/retail publishing of fiction and non-fiction, educational publishing, and academic and scientific publishing.
Who is credited with discovering Glutathione?
Glutathione: Frederick Hopkins. Glutathione (GSH,) is a tripeptide made of the amino acids glutamate, cysteine, and glycine.
Who is credited with discovering Blockchain?
Blockchain: Satoshi Nakamoto. A blockchain is a distributed ledger with growing lists of records (blocks) that are securely linked together via cryptographic hashes.
Who is credited with discovering Ethology?
Ethology: Isidore Geoffroy Saint-Hilaire. Ethology is a branch of zoology that studies the behaviour of non-human animals.
Sitting atop the kidneys, this pair of endocrine glands produces hormones including adrenaline, aldosterone, and cortisol. What organ is it?
Adrenal gland (also known as suprarenal glands) are endocrine glands that produce a variety of hormones including adrenaline and the steroids aldosterone and cortisol.
Formed naturally around volcanic vents and on burning coal dumps, this soluble white crystalline salt serves as both a fertilizer and a food additive — what's the compound with formula NH4Cl?
Ammonium chloride is an inorganic chemical compound with the chemical formula NH4Cl, also written as Cl.
Fill in the blank: “____ (April 21, 1971 - September 30, 2011) was an American-Yemeni Islamic cleric and lecturer.”

Anwar al-Awlaki (April 21, 1971 - September 30, 2011) was an American-Yemeni Islamic cleric and lecturer. Al-Awlaki was the first U.S. citizen to be targeted and assassinated by a U.S. government drone strike.
Part of the family Ericaceae, these shrubs flower in April and May in the Northern Hemisphere and October and November south of the equator — what are they called?
Azalea (-) are flowering shrubs in the genus Rhododendron, particularly the former subgenera Tsutsusi (evergreen) and Pentanthera (deciduous).
This red-orange compound, formed from the breakdown of heme, is further processed into pigments that give feces their brown color and urine its straw-yellow hue. What is it?
Bilirubin (BR) (adopted from German, originally bili, for bile, plus ruber, Latin for red) is a red-orange compound that occurs as the reduction product of biliverdin, a breakdown product of heme.

Making up only about 2.6 percent of the brain's total weight, this stalk-like structure connects the cerebrum to the spinal cord and regulates critical functions like heart rate and breathing. What is it called?
Brainstem (or brain stem) is the posterior stalk-like part of the brain that connects the cerebrum with the spinal cord.
This biological family includes domestic dogs, wolves, coyotes, foxes, and jackals, found on every continent except Antarctica. What family is it?
Canidae (from Latin, canis, "dog") is a biological family of caniform carnivorans, constituting a clade.
Despite no clinical evidence it treats any disease, this daisy-like plant is a staple in calming herbal tea, beer brewing, and even garden ground cover — what is it?
Chamomile (American English) or camomile (British English; see spelling differences) (or) is the common name for several daisy-like plants of the family Asteraceae.
This neurological disorder strikes one side of the head around the eye and temple, often at the very same hour each day for an 8-to-10-week stretch before vanishing for months — what condition is it?
Cluster headache is a neurological disorder characterized by episodes of severe headaches on one side of the head, typically around the eye and temple, lasting between 15 minutes to three hours.
Which genus of passerine birds, whose Latin name literally means 'raven,' includes about 46 species commonly known as crows, ravens, and rooks?
Corvus is a widely distributed genus of passerine birds ranging from medium-sized to large-sized in the family Corvidae.
Affecting some 280 million people worldwide, this state of low mood saps motivation and the pleasure once taken in activities — what is it?
Depression (mood) is a mental state of low mood and aversion to activity.

This hypothetical megastructure would encircle an entire star to capture most of its energy output, conceived as a thought experiment for how an advanced civilization might meet growing power needs — what's the concept called?
Dyson sphere is a hypothetical megastructure that encompasses a star and captures a large percentage of its power output.
With a US prevalence of about 8.2 cases per million births, this inherited disorder can cause complications from esophageal narrowing to skin cancer to amputation — which condition?
Epidermolysis bullosa (EB) is a group of rare medical conditions that result in easy blistering of the skin and mucous membranes.
A Swiss linguist and philosopher who died in 1913, this thinker's ideas shaped 20th-century linguistics, psychoanalysis, and anthropology alike, according to one of his translators — who is he?
Ferdinand de Saussure (26 November 1857 - 22 February 1913) was a Swiss linguist, semiotician and philosopher.
Its name comes from Greek for 'milk flower,' and this small genus of about 20 bulbous perennials nods with a single white bell of six tepals — what is the botanical name for the snowdrop?
Galanthus (from Ancient Greek, (gla, "milk") + (nthos, "flower")), or snowdrop, is a small genus of approximately 20 species of bulbous perennial herbaceous plants in the family Amaryllidaceae.

Found in northern South America, this tarantula is the world's heaviest and longest-bodied spider, tipping the scales at over 170 grams, though a huntsman spider still beats it on leg span — what spider is it?
Goliath birdeater (Theraphosa blondi) is a large spider that belongs to the tarantula family Theraphosidae.

This now-outdated astronomical model placed the Sun rather than the Earth at the center of the universe, eventually replacing the geocentric view before itself being superseded by relativity — what model is it?
Heliocentrism (also known as the heliocentric model) is a superseded astronomical model that placed the Sun at the center of the universe, with the Earth and the planets in its orbit.
With atomic number 1, this element's most common isotope holds just one proton and one electron, and it's what stars like the Sun mainly burn — what is it?
Hydrogen is a chemical element; it has the symbol H and atomic number 1.
Many plants stockpile this energy-storing polysaccharide in their roots instead of starch, and doctors still use it as the benchmark substance for testing kidney function — name the fiber?
Inulin are a group of naturally occurring polysaccharides produced by many types of plants, industrially most often extracted from chicory.
This financier's 1999 bestseller on mutual funds became an investment classic after he founded a low-cost investing giant — who is he?

John C. Bogle (May 8, 1929 - January 16, 2019) was an American investor, business magnate and philanthropist who was the founder of The Vanguard Group and is credited with popularizing the index fund.
This Arab dessert layers spun pastry dough with cheese, soaked in a sugar syrup, with its most famous variant hailing from the Palestinian city of Nablus — what is it?
Knafeh is a traditional Arab dessert made with kadayif (spun pastry dough) layered with cheese and soaked in a sweet, sugar-based syrup called attar.
This big-cat hybrid, born of a male lion and a female tiger, is the largest of all living cats, growing larger than either parent and enjoying a swim. What animal is it?
Liger is a hybrid offspring of a male lion (Panthera leo) and a tigress, or female tiger (Panthera tigris).

Developed by MathWorks, this proprietary programming language and numeric computing environment is built around matrix manipulation, and pairs with an add-on called Simulink for graphical simulation and model-based design. What software is this?
MATLAB (Matrix Laboratory) is a proprietary multi-paradigm programming language and numeric computing environment developed by MathWorks.
A German historian, jurist, and political economist born in 1864, he is counted among the central founders of sociology and still shapes social theory today — who was he?

Max Weber (21 April 1864 - 14 June 1920) was a German sociologist, historian, jurist, and political economist who was one of the central figures in the development of sociology and the social sciences more generally.
This unit of time, normally equal to 60 seconds, can rarely stretch to 61 seconds under the UTC time standard because of a leap second — what is it?
Minute (symbol: min) is a unit of time defined as equal to 60 seconds.

This European twin-engine military helicopter was the first production helicopter ever built with entirely fly-by-wire flight controls, coming in both troop-transport and naval anti-submarine variants — what aircraft is it?
NHIndustries NH90 is a medium-sized European twin-engine multi-role military helicopter.
Which Turkish-born American economist, an NYU Stern professor, earned lasting fame as one of the few who predicted the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis?
Nouriel Roubini (born March 29, 1958) is a Turkish-born American economic consultant, economist, speaker, and writer.
Also called trioxygen and far less stable than the oxygen we breathe, it carries the formula O3 and smells faintly of chlorine — what is this gas?
Ozone is an inorganic molecule with the chemical formula O3.
What medical term describes damage or disease affecting the nerves — impairing sensation, movement, gland, or organ function — commonly caused by systemic diseases such as diabetes?

Peripheral neuropathy is damage or disease affecting the nerves. Peripheral neuropathy may be acute (with sudden onset, rapid progress) or chronic (symptoms begin subtly and progress slowly), and may be reversible or permanent.
This zodiac sign's Latin name means 'fishes,' and it's where the ecliptic crosses the celestial equator near the March equinox — which one?
Pisces (constellation) is a constellation of the zodiac. It is between Aquarius, of similar size, to the southwest and Aries, which is smaller, to the east.
This Danish midfielder won three Eredivisie titles at Ajax before being twice named his London club's Player of the Year during a six-year spell there. Who is he?
Priapism is a condition in which a penis remains erect for hours in the absence of stimulation or after stimulation has ended.
It can form not just from rain but from mist, spray, or dew, and though we usually see an arc, it can actually be a full circle — what optical phenomenon is it?
Rainbow is an optical phenomenon caused by refraction, internal reflection and dispersion of light in water droplets resulting in a continuous spectrum of light appearing in the sky.
Known by the common name 'dog rose,' this climbing wild rose species is native across Europe and stretches into northwest Africa and western Asia — which species?
Rosa canina is a variable climbing, wild rose species native to Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia.
Which leathery-skinned marine echinoderm, of which about 1,786 species are known worldwide, plays a vital ecological role on the sea floor by breaking down detritus as a scavenger?
Sea cucumber are echinoderms from the class Holothuroidea.
This group of nocturnal Southeast Asian primates ranges from Yunnan province in China down to the island of Java, with a pygmy relative recently reclassified into its own genus — what are they?
Slow loris are a group of several species of nocturnal strepsirrhine primates that make up the genus Nycticebus.
Innervated by the accessory nerve, which of the body's largest and most superficial neck structures rotates the head to the opposite side and flexes the neck?
Sternocleidomastoid muscle is one of the largest and most superficial cervical muscles.
This actress and singer's breakout role on Pretty Little Liars won her seven Teen Choice Awards, more than any actress in a single series. Who is she?
Tarragon (Artemisia dracunculus), also known as estragon, is a species of perennial herb in the family Asteraceae.
This intensely itchy, contagious fungal skin infection produces a red, scaly rash with a curved border across the groin and buttocks, mostly in men — what is it?

Tinea cruris (TC), also known as jock itch, is a common type of contagious, superficial fungal infection of the groin and buttocks region, which occurs predominantly but not exclusively in men and in hot-humid climates.
A byproduct of purine breakdown normally found in urine, elevated blood levels of this heterocyclic compound can cause gout and kidney stones — what's the compound (C5H4N4O3)?
Uric acid is a heterocyclic compound of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, and hydrogen with the formula C5H4N4O3.
These big cetaceans — everything in the group except dolphins and porpoises — count the hippopotamus as their closest living relative on land. What are they?
Whale are a widely distributed and diverse group of fully aquatic placental marine mammals.

Unlike a user interface, which links a computer to a person, this software connection lets programs talk directly to each other — and the standard describing it is called its specification. What's the three-letter term?
API: Connection between computers or programs.
Nicknamed the 'killer' variety for its aggressive defense of the hive, this hybrid pollinating insect escaped Brazilian quarantine in 1957 and reached Texas by 1990 — which insect is it?
Africanized bee: Hybrid species of bee. The African honey bee was first introduced to Brazil in 1956 to increase honey production, but 26 swarms escaped quarantine in 1957.
Unlike its bulb-forming relative, the common onion, this perennial vegetable never forms a bulb and owes one of its names to its hollow, tube-like leaves — which plant?
Allium fistulosum: Species of plant. The species is very similar in taste and odor to the related common onion, Allium cepa, and hybrids between the two (tree onions) exist.
This Russian physicist miraculously survived a 1978 accident in which a high-energy proton beam from a particle accelerator passed directly through his skull — who is he?
Anatoli Bugorski: Soviet and Russian scientist (born 1942)
Lacking a tail due to a mutation in the TBXT gene, this superfamily of primates includes gibbons as the 'lesser' branch and humans among the 'great' branch — which animal group?
Ape: Superfamily of primates. The family Hylobatidae, the lesser apes, include four genera and a total of 20 species of gibbon, including the lar gibbon and the siamang, all native to Asia.
First described in 1740 under the name Compositae, this enormous flowering-plant family includes daisies, asters and sunflowers — what is it?
Asteraceae: Large family of flowering plants.
A sessile marine arthropod related to crabs and lobsters, folklore once claimed geese hatched fully formed from one variety of it — what creature is it?
Barnacle: Subclass of sessile marine crustaceans.
This English musician played bass on the Rolling Stones' first nineteen studio albums across three decades before later fronting his own blues outfit, the Rhythm Kings — who is he?

A twin-engine, carrier-capable strike fighter flown by the U.S., Australia, and Kuwait, this larger, more advanced follow-on to an earlier 1980s Navy jet packs an internal 20 mm rotary cannon and can be rigged as an airborne refueling tanker — what is it called?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Boeing F/A-18E/F Super Hornet: Series of carrier-based multirole combat aircraft.
Despite the name, this pseudocereal isn't related to true cereals at all — it's kin to rhubarb and sorrel, and was first cultivated in Yunnan around 6,000 BC — which crop is it?
Buckwheat: Species of flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae.
This suborder of 'dog-like' carnivores includes bears, raccoons, weasels, and seals, and is thought to have diversified mainly across North America and northern Eurasia — what's it called?
Caniformia: Suborder of mammals. Caniformia is a suborder within the order Carnivora consisting of "dog-like" carnivorans.
Named for barbels that resemble a cat's whiskers, these scaleless, ray-finned fish include giants like the Mekong species and go by nicknames such as 'mud cat' in the Southern US — what are they?
Catfish: Order of fish. Catfish are a diverse group of ray-finned fish of the order Siluriformes (historically Nematognathi).

One of the earliest cultivated legumes — its oldest traces were unearthed in Syria — this protein-packed seed goes by names like garbanzo and chana, and forms the backbone of hummus and falafel. What is it?
Chickpea: Species of flowering plant with edible seeds.
This English inventor made the world's first slimline pocket calculator in 1972, then launched the UK's first mass-market home computer for under £100 — who is he?
Clive Sinclair: English entrepreneur and inventor (1940–2021)
A heavy-set, fox-like canid native to East Asia, this animal is named for its raccoon-like face markings and is unusual among canids for hibernating in winter and climbing trees. What is this animal?
Common raccoon dog: Canid indigenous to East Asia. Named for its raccoon-like face markings, it is most closely related to foxes.

An incurable, always fatal neurodegenerative disease belonging to the transmissible spongiform encephalopathy group, it causes early symptoms like memory problems, behavioral changes, and poor coordination, with about 70% of sufferers dying within a year. What disease is it?
Known as Queen Anne's lace, this Old World wildflower is the wild ancestor of the cultivated carrot — what is it?
Daucus carota: Species of flowering plant.
A Cambridge-educated lecturer in English literature, this Hashemite princess briefly reigned as Queen of Jordan as King Hussein's first wife — who is she?
Dina bint Abdul-Hamid: Queen of Jordan from 1955 to 1957.
Known as 'crawling' pinnipeds to distinguish them from their eared, sea-lion-like cousins, this group's only completely freshwater population lives in Lake Baikal — what are they called?
This branch of biology and medicine studies the glands that secrete hormones directly into the bloodstream, governing everything from growth to mood and metabolism — what is it called?
Endocrinology: Branch of medicine pertaining to the endocrine system.
Commonly called spurge, this giant plant genus includes the popular Christmas poinsettia and a thorny succulent nicknamed 'crown of thorns' — which genus is it?
This subfamily of cats, distinguished by a bony hyoid that lets its members purr instead of roar, is informally known as the small cats — which subfamily?
Felinae: Subfamily of Felidae. The Felinae or small cats are a subfamily of the Felidae distinguished by a bony hyoid, because of which they can purr but not roar.
This infection and inflammation of hair follicles produces pimples with white tips anywhere on hair-covered skin — what is the condition called?
Folliculitis: Human and animal disease of follicles.
Once classified under two different bacterial genera, this nonmotile coccobacillus forms small gray colonies on chocolate agar and has its own colistin-oxolinic acid selective medium — which species?
Gardnerella vaginalis: Species of bacterium. Gardnerella vaginalis is a species of Gram-variable-staining facultative anaerobic bacteria.
Nicknamed the "silent thief of sight" because it steals vision slowly, this group of eye diseases damages the optic nerve and is closely tied to raised pressure inside the eye — what is it?
Glaucoma: Group of eye diseases related to poor retinal and nerve perfusion.
With long, whip-like antennae and a global range except Antarctica, this insect family — known as true crickets — includes burrowing giants that dig meter-deep tunnels. What is the family called?
Gryllidae: Family of crickets. The family Gryllidae contains the subfamilies and genera which entomologists now term true crickets.
Native to North America, this genus of roughly 50 flowering plant species is better known by its common name — the sunflowers — and includes food crops for humans and livestock alike — which genus?

Helianthus: Genus of flowering plants, the sunflowers. Helianthus is a genus comprising around 50 species of annual and perennial flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae commonly known as sunflowers.
This genus of great apes emerged from Australopithecus and includes modern humans alongside extinct relatives, with chimpanzees and bonobos as its closest living kin — what genus is it?
Homo: Genus of hominins. Homo erectus and Homo neanderthalensis) classified as either ancestral or closely related to modern humans, collectively called archaic humans.

When the thyroid gland churns out too much hormone, the result can be a racing heartbeat, heat intolerance, hand tremor and weight loss — and rarely, a life-threatening 'thyroid storm.' What is this condition?
Hyperthyroidism: Excessive production of thyroid hormone.

Marked by an IQ below 70 and deficits in everyday adaptive skills first apparent in childhood, this neurodevelopmental condition was formerly called 'mental retardation' in the U.S. — what is it now called?
Known as sampaguita in the Philippines, where it's the national flower, this fragrant vine or shrub also lends its blossoms to a beloved variety of tea — which species?
Jasminum sambac: Species of jasmine. Jasminum sambac (Arabian jasmine or Sambac jasmine or Mogra) is a species of jasmine native to Bhutan and India.
Also nicknamed the reed or swamp feline, this solitary wild predator ranges from the Caucasus to Southeast Asia and marks territory by urine spraying — which species?
This severe form of childhood protein malnutrition causes swelling and an enlarged, fatty liver, and is distinct from the calorie-deficient condition known as marasmus — what is it?
Kwashiorkor: Severe protein malnutrition. Kwashiorkor ( KWOSH-ee-OR-kor, -⁠kər) is a form of severe protein malnutrition characterized by edema and an enlarged liver with fatty infiltrates.
Marked by weariness and a desire to act without the energy to do so, which condition can be a normal response to poor sleep or stress, or a sign of underlying illness?
Lethargy: State of tiredness, weariness, fatigue, or lack of energy.
Reaching about 200 kg at its largest, this reddish-brown-shelled reptile ranges through the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans as well as the Mediterranean — which species?
Loggerhead sea turtle: Species of marine reptile distributed throughout the world.
A former mayor of Tehran and engineer by training, he served as Iran's sixth president from 2005 to 2013 and championed the country's nuclear program — who is he?

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad: President of Iran from 2005 to 2013. Mahmoud Ahmadinejad (né Sabbaghian; born 28 October 1956) is an Iranian politician who served as the sixth president of Iran from 2005 to 2013.

Belonging to the ancient order Ephemeroptera and keeping primitive traits like long tails and wings that won't fold flat, which aquatic insect's water-dwelling nymphs signal a clean, unpolluted stream?
Mayfly: Aquatic insects of the order Ephemeroptera. Over 3,000 species of mayfly are known worldwide, grouped into over 400 genera in 42 families.
This colorless gas, made by swapping one hydrogen atom in ammonia for a methyl group, has a strong rotten-fish smell and serves as a building block for many compounds — what is it?
Native to Southeast Asia, this evergreen tree's leaves are known as kratom, containing alkaloids that bind to opioid receptors — which species?
Mitragyna speciosa: Species of plant. It is under preliminary research for possible antipsychotic and antidepressant properties.
Taking its name from the Latin for 'weasel,' this is the largest family in the suborder Caniformia — gathering otters, badgers, martens, and wolverines under one roof. What is it?
Described by Eric Kandel as the 'epic challenge' of biology, this multidisciplinary field studies the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nervous system — what field is it?
Neuroscience: Scientific study of the nervous system.
This condition of involuntary eye movement can be triggered by stimulating the ear's semicircular canals — for example with the caloric test — while the head stays still. What is it?
Nystagmus: Dysfunction of eye movement. Nystagmus is a condition of involuntary (or voluntary, in some cases) eye movement.
This surgical medical subspecialty treats the ear, nose, and throat — organs connected via the Eustachian tube — earning its specialists the nickname 'ENT surgeons.' What field is it?
Otorhinolaryngology: Medical specialty of the head and neck.
From the Greek for 'the study of disease,' this medical field diagnoses illness largely by analyzing tissue and cell samples — what is it?
Pathology: Study of disease. The word pathology also refers to the study of disease in general, incorporating a wide range of biology research fields and medical practices.
What is the process by which immune cells like macrophages and neutrophils engulf pathogens and debris with their plasma membrane, forming an internal compartment called a phagosome?
Phagocytosis: Cell membrane engulfing a large particle.
This self-limiting skin condition begins with a single “herald patch” before smaller scaly spots erupt days later, usually clearing up on its own within three months — which condition?
Pityriasis rosea: Skin disease. It usually lasts less than three months and goes away without treatment.
Used to disinfect skin before and after surgery, this antiseptic can cause kidney problems and high blood sodium if applied to large wounds, and comes as a liquid, ointment, or powder — what is it?
Povidone-iodine: Antiseptic solution. Povidone-iodine (PVP-I), also known as iodopovidone, is an antiseptic used for skin disinfection before and after surgery.

Covering the asymmetric relationship between citizens and the state — including constitutional, administrative, tax, and criminal matters — this branch of the legal system contrasts with the branch governing relationships between individuals — which branch?
Public law: Law governing government actions.
Native to the southern United States, this pond terrapin is the world's most commonly traded and most invasive turtle, largely due to pet releases — which species?
This American neuroscientist and primatologist, a Stanford professor across three departments, has spent his career studying the neuroendocrinology of stress — who is he?
The largest genus in the mint family, this group of nearly 1,000 shrubs and herbs includes common cooking sage and rosemary — what's the genus called?
Salvia: Largest genus of plants in the mint family. Salvia is the largest genus of plants in the sage family Lamiaceae, with just under 1,000 species of shrubs, herbaceous perennials, and annuals.
A peptide mimicking a gut hormone, this drug treats type 2 diabetes as Ozempic and Rybelsus but is sold as Wegovy for weight loss — what's the underlying medication?
Related to polecats but more closely kin to the Old World stink badgers, these black-and-white mammals defend themselves by spraying a foul-smelling liquid from their anal glands — which animal?
Skunk: Common name of mammals in the family Mephitidae.
Acting as a blood filter and red-blood-cell recycling center, which vertebrate organ also stores a reserve of blood for use during hemorrhagic shock?
Spleen: Immune organ that filters blood.
NATO nicknamed this Soviet variable-sweep-wing tactical bomber 'Fencer'; it was the USSR's first plane with an integrated digital navigation-and-attack system — which aircraft is it?
Sukhoi Su-24: Family of Soviet strike aircraft.
Once the thylacine went extinct in 1936, this stocky, screeching marsupial — now confined to a single island — became the world's largest carnivorous marsupial; what is it?
